# Minimum and maximum

The smallest and largest elements of a slice, and clamping a value into a range.

<h2 id="min-index"><code>MinIndex&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func MinIndex<T>(items: T[..]) -> uint?
```

The index of the smallest element of `items`.
`items` is borrowed and read. Reports `none` for an empty slice, and the earliest index when several elements
tie.
Requires `<` on the element type.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length, comparing each element once, and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/MinMax.rux#L22)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |

**Returns**: the index of the smallest element, the first when several tie, or `none` when empty

<h2 id="min-index-by"><code>MinIndexBy&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func MinIndexBy<T>(
    items: T[..],
    compare: func(T, T) -> Ordering
) -> uint?
```

The index of the smallest element of `items`, with `compare` deciding.
`items` is borrowed and read; `compare` is called once per element after the first. Reports `none` for an empty
slice, and the earliest index when several elements tie.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `compare` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/MinMax.rux#L66)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                     | Description                               |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`                  | the sequence to work on                   |
| `compare` | `func(T, T) -> Ordering` | how two elements order against each other |

**Returns**: the index of the smallest element under `compare`, or `none` when empty

<h2 id="min-max-index"><code>MinMaxIndex&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func MinMaxIndex<T>(
    items: T[..],
    smallest: *var uint,
    largest: *var uint
) -> bool
```

The indices of the smallest and largest elements of `items`, in one pass.
`items` is borrowed and read; `smallest` and `largest` are written only when this reports true. Reports false for
an empty slice and writes neither. Ties go to the earliest index on both ends, exactly as the single-ended
searches promise.
Two separate passes would compare each element twice; this compares them in pairs and so makes about three
comparisons for every two elements.
Requires `<` on the element type.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.
`smallest` and `largest` must be non-null and writable.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/MinMax.rux#L116)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type        | Description                                |
| ---------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `items`    | `T[..]`     | the sequence to work on                    |
| `smallest` | `*var uint` | receives the index of the smallest element |
| `largest`  | `*var uint` | receives the index of the largest element  |

**Returns**: whether there was anything to report, which an empty sequence is not

<h2 id="min"><code>Min&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Min<T>(left: T, right: T) -> T
```

The smaller of two values, or `left` when neither is smaller.
Both are read by value and one is returned by copy. Requires `<` on the type.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/MinMax.rux#L175)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type | Description           |
| ------- | ---- | --------------------- |
| `left`  | `T`  | one of the two values |
| `right` | `T`  | the other             |

**Returns**: the smaller of the two, or `left` when they tie

<h2 id="max"><code>Max&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Max<T>(left: T, right: T) -> T
```

The larger of two values, or `left` when neither is larger.
Both are read by value and one is returned by copy. Requires `<` on the type.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the larger of the two, or `left` when they tie

<h2 id="clamp"><code>Clamp&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Clamp<T>(value: T, low: T, high: T) -> T
```

`value` brought into the range `low` to `high`, inclusive at both ends.
All three are read by value and one is returned by copy. A `low` above `high` is an empty range with no answer
that could be right, so `low` is returned — the caller passed a range it cannot have meant.
Requires `<` on the type.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/MinMax.rux#L204)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type | Description                   |
| ------- | ---- | ----------------------------- |
| `value` | `T`  | the value to bring into range |
| `low`   | `T`  | the lowest allowed value      |
| `high`  | `T`  | the highest allowed value     |

**Returns**: `value` brought into `[low, high]`

<h2 id="clamp-by"><code>ClampBy&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ClampBy<T>(
    value: T,
    low: T,
    high: T,
    compare: func(T, T) -> Ordering
) -> T
```

`value` brought into the range `low` to `high`, with `compare` deciding.
All three values are read by value and one is returned by copy; `compare` is called at most three times. A `low`
above `high` returns `low`, exactly as [`Clamp`](/docs/api/algorithms/min-max#clamp) does.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing beyond whatever `compare` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/MinMax.rux#L222)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                     | Description                               |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `value`   | `T`                      | the value to bring into range             |
| `low`     | `T`                      | the lowest allowed value                  |
| `high`    | `T`                      | the highest allowed value                 |
| `compare` | `func(T, T) -> Ordering` | how two elements order against each other |

**Returns**: `value` brought into `[low, high]` under `compare`
